substantive_reconstruction.universal_linear_schur: For an F-linear intertwiner between nonzero algebraically irreducible V,W, kernel and image are invariant linear subspaces. A nonzero map has a proper kernel and nonzero image, so irreducibility gives kernel0 and imageW. This is actual algebraic surjectivity even in infinite dimension, not an invalid rank-nullity shortcut. The inverse is linear; multiplying f rho_V(g)=rho_W(g)f by f^-1 verifies its equivariance. The word endomorphism is correctly linear, not every equivariant function.
substantive_reconstruction.division_ring_and_dimension: End_G(V) is closed under addition/composition/scalars and contains nonzero identity for V!=0. Every nonzero element has its commuting linear inverse by part(i), so it is a division ring. Scalar maps give an injected central F because V is nonzero and all endomorphisms are F-linear. Commutativity or equality with F does not follow. If V is finite-dimensional, this commutant is an F-linear subspace of End_F(V), hence dimension at most(dim V)^2; that bound is not transported to arbitrary V.
substantive_reconstruction.real_C4_and_full_commutant: J=[[0,-1],[1,0]] has J^2=-I,J^4=I, defining C4. Any proper nonzero invariant real subspace in R^2 is a line, so Jv=a v would imply-v=a^2 v, impossible over R. For A=[[p,q],[r,s]], AJ=[[q,-p],[s,-r]] and JA=[[-r,-s],[p,q]] give p=s,r=-q. Hence ALL commuting matrices, not merely a subalgebra of examples, are aI+bJ=[[a,-b],[b,a]]. Multiplication follows J^2=-I, giving a bijective real-algebra identification with C. Determinant a^2+b^2 and inverse(aI-bJ)/(a^2+b^2) check the division property. J is nonscalar; over C it has eigenlines and this real irreducibility does not persist.
substantive_reconstruction.scalar_conditional_and_not_iff: For finite positive-dimensional V over algebraically closed F, each commuting f has a base-field eigenvalue lambda by its positive-degree characteristic polynomial. The commuting f-lambda I has nonzero kernel, hence part(i) forces it0, so f=lambda I. The proof uses no finite group or characteristic-zero averaging. For a particular arbitrary-dimensional module, an eigenvalue for each f also suffices. If each f is algebraic over an algebraically closed central F, a nonzero split annihilating polynomial gives a product of(f-lambda I) factors equal0, and the division ring's lack of zero divisors forces a vanishing factor. These are sufficient interfaces, not an iff demand for finite dimension or algebraic closure. A real line has scalar real commutant despite R not algebraically closed.
substantive_reconstruction.full_rational_function_commutant: Let K=C(t), G=K^times and V=K over C. Multiplication is complex-linear, invertible and respects the group law. Powers1,t,t^2,... are independent since t is an indeterminate. If an invariant nonzero complex subspace contains w, each v!=0 is(gw) with g=v/w, proving genuine algebraic irreducibility. If f commutes with all multiplications, then for v!=0, f(v)=f(M_v1)=M_v f(1)=v f(1), and f0=0 by linearity. Conversely every M_a commutes, so the ENTIRE commutant is K, not simply known to contain K. M_t is nonscalar; M_t-lambda I has inverse M_(1/(t-lambda)) for every complex lambda. This directly disproves unrestricted algebraically-closed scalar collapse. Replacing C by R yields R(t), so an unrestricted R/C/H exhaustion is likewise false.
